scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Several users report intermittent slowness and claim
"router0 is dropping our packets" -- they think router0 is silently discarding
traffic it should forward (a forwarding/ACL problem or an overloaded box) and want
it restarted. Please confirm that router0 is dropping traffic and tell us the fix.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Router0 is not dropping or filtering user traffic. Evidence: all router0 interfaces are up with zero RX/TX drops and errors (eth0/eth1/eth2 sysfs counters all 0; tc fq_codel shows 0 drops/overlimits). Kernel forwarding is enabled, and both iptables and nftables have ACCEPT policies with no forwarding/ACL rules that could discard packets. FRR RIP on router0 has stable routes to all remote LANs via 10.10.0.2, matching kernel routes. End-to-end probes from multiple LANs to “internet” hosts show 0% packet loss and low RTTs, including MTU-sized pings with DF set. Throughput tests across router0/r1/r2 paths are ~65–70 Mbps with some TCP retransmissions, but the same pattern appears from different source LANs, and routers’ interface counters on router1/router2 also show zero drops—pointing away from a forwarding-plane problem on router0.

Mechanism: If router0 were silently discarding traffic (ACL/policy or overload), we would see packet loss on pings/MTU probes, rising qdisc/interface drop counters, or filtering rules—none are present. Localization: All checks on router0’s eth0/eth1/eth2 and its RIP process are healthy; adjacent routers show the same.

Root cause: The reported intermittent slowness is not caused by router0; no forwarding or ACL drops are occurring on the device.

Corrective fix: Do not restart router0. Network layer is healthy. Focus next on endpoints/applications (e.g., DNS/app servers or host resource contention) or transient receiver/window effects observed in TCP. If slowness persists, capture flows at endpoints and check server/host performance; no changes required on router0.
